sets.title: Bitvector arithmetic and complete bounds

objective_text.T61.01.a: Derive and defend: Derive the pre-add inequality without executing overflowing signed arithmetic. Prove unchanged output on failure as a separate postcondition and identify pointer validity assumptions.
objective_text.T61.01.b: Implement and investigate: Implement vf_add(a,b,out) for uint32_t: return1 and sum when representable, else0 with unchanged output. Write a CBMC harness for every input and a sentinel output, with overflow checks enabled; separately exhaust a reduced8-bit domain and explain why that enumeration is not a proof for32-bit implementation code.
objective_text.T61.01.c: Falsify and transfer: Repair wrapping arithmetic that reports success and a harness that assumes away every overflow input. Demonstrate a witness satisfying the assumptions and violating the mutant. Then Generalize to checked multiplication and mixed-width conversion, deriving a new precondition rather than mechanically substituting the addition predicate.

sets.title: Loop invariants and binary-search termination

objective_text.T61.02.a: Derive and defend: Prove all indices below lo are<key, all at/above hi are>=key, and hi-lo strictly decreases. Derive memory bounds and handle duplicate values without changing the intended first-position contract.
objective_text.T61.02.b: Implement and investigate: Implement vf_lower_bound on a sorted nondecreasing uint32_t array, returning the first index with value>=key or n. Use half-open[lo,hi), calculate midpoint without overflow and retain O(log n) comparisons. Empty input permits a null array. Establish sortedness as a precondition, not a fact proved by a search test.
objective_text.T61.02.c: Falsify and transfer: A <= comparison implements upper_bound, which passes unique-key examples. An incorrect midpoint update can also loop forever on a singleton interval. Then Change to a descending comparator and an opaque record key; rederive the invariant and verify comparator consistency assumptions instead of copying inequalities.

objective_text.T61.03.a: Derive and defend: Prove size conservation and rejection atomicity at each step; define ownership of queued elements separately from the scalar ring indices. Explain why an oracle sharing the same count representation could reproduce the defect.
objective_text.T61.03.b: Implement and investigate: Implement vf_ring_step for VFRing with positive capacity, head<capacity, size<=capacity. op0 push rejects full and increments size; op1 pop rejects empty, advances head modulo capacity and decrements size. Reject invalid state or operation without mutation. Build a sequence harness using a Python list oracle and generation from valid/invalid transition classes.
objective_text.T61.03.c: Falsify and transfer: The mutant permits a push into a full ring, producing size>capacity. A final pop-only test can conceal this intermediate violation. Then Add borrowed payloads with destructor callbacks and injected construction failure; extend the model to exactly-once lifetime obligations and reentrant callback restrictions.

sets.title: Parser fuzzing with semantic oracles

objective_text.T61.04.a: Derive and defend: Separate memory-safety, grammar, integrity and canonicalization properties; bound fuzz input processing without excluding empty, malformed or huge harness inputs.
objective_text.T61.04.b: Implement and investigate: Implement vf_frame for bytes[length,payload...,xor]. Require n>=2, length<=16, exact n=length+2 and XOR of payload equal final byte; publish length only on success. Empty payload is valid with bytes[0,0]. Fuzz all inputs0..64 bytes, check round-trip canonical encoding on success and output sentinel on failure.
objective_text.T61.04.c: Falsify and transfer: The parser ignores checksum mismatch yet never crashes, so sanitizer-only fuzzing misses the defect. The semantic oracle must reject the corrupted frame. Then Introduce streaming segmentation and state reset between repeated calls; compare every split with the single-shot decoder and minimize a split-sensitive mismatch.

sets.title: Counterexample minimization

objective_text.T61.05.a: Derive and defend: Prove predicate preservation after each deletion and justify termination. Distinguish1-minimality from globally optimal shrinking and discuss order-dependent outcomes.
objective_text.T61.05.b: Implement and investigate: Implement vf_shrink for an in-place byte vector of length at most65535 whose failure predicate is sum(bytes)>=threshold. Greedily remove each byte when the remaining sum still fails; retry the same position after removal. Return final length. If the original does not fail, leave it unchanged. The result is1-minimal under deletion, not globally shortest.
objective_text.T61.05.c: Falsify and transfer: The faulty shrinker increments its index after deletion, skipping the shifted byte and leaving a removable element. A merely smaller result is not the stated minimality guarantee. Then Shrink an event schedule while preserving the same violated lifecycle invariant and first divergent transition, rather than preserving any nonzero exit.

objective_text.T61.06.b: Implement and investigate: Implement vf_request for events0 submit,1 cancel,2 complete,3 release. Submit once; cancellation only after submit and before completion; complete once after submit whether or not cancelled; release only after completion and only once. objective_text.T61.07.a: Derive and defend: Derive the required isolation between fuzz invocations, including allocator cleanup and thread joining. Distinguish deterministic input-derived randomness from wall-clock seeding.
objective_text.T61.07.b: Implement and investigate: Implement vf_digest(frame,n,out): validate with vf_frame, then derive a32-bit rolling digest starting from0 for that input only, digest=digest*33+byte across payload bytes. Preserve output on invalid input. Repeated A,B,A calls must give the same results for A. Keep corpus generation and sanitizer runtime outside the target dependency graph.
